svg.title: Immunocompromised host decision chart: fever or illness sorted by presentation and immune defect into the opportunistic infections tuberculosis, Mycobacterium avium complex, Pneumocystis pneumonia, Cryptococcus and cytomegalovirus, each with clues, investigations in order and management, with the timing of risk after stem cell transplant and how to prevent infection

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Fever in an IMMUNOCOMPROMISED host: which DEFECT, and which OPPORTUNIST does it let in?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: the usual differential + OPPORTUNISTIC infections + context: immune deficiency is dynamic, TIMING is everything

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: STEM CELL transplant: weeks 3–4 Gram-negatives · > 3 months (CD4 last) encapsulated bacteria, fungi, viruses

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: the presentation is blunted: fever may be ABSENT on cytokine blockers (anakinra, rilonacept, tocilizumab, anti-TNF)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: PREVENT: vaccinate BEFORE immunosuppression (LIVE vaccines generally unsafe) · no vaccine → PROPHYLAXIS

svg.text: • cough > 3 weeks + TB risk, ANY CD4 count → TB

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: • structural lung disease, or HIV with CD4 < 50 → MAC
